what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the start-a-computer folder: make a machine into a computer that keeps people's accounts, read its price, its state and the health page at its name, check that it takes a new account end to end, and give it back. The provider is a description file the person keeps outside this folder, named by machine.provider (and name.provider) in the request; the provider's credential reaches the one process on a private pipe (descriptor 3, the name provider's on descriptor 4).

payload.label: Start a computer
payload.job: Make a machine into a computer that runs what its own row says: rent one or use one I already run, set it up, build its programs from source there and read back its health page
payload.description: Rents a machine from the provider description the request names (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through the name provider description, and applies the computer's own row (record:computer, `runs`) over SSH: set-up (packages, toolchains, users, folders, keys), each unit with a `source` fetched by the machine itself from the git address the row names and built there (no release, no feed, no copied program), the files the row renders, the restarts and each unit's boot check. Answers the lease, the machine's architecture, the monthly price, what the apply wrote, built and restarted, and the public health page's HTTP status. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

request_file.description: A request JSON (lease_file, machine, name, ssh, computer_row or computer_row_file, pages_folder when the row's caddy names pages_root); local paths are read relative to it.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Hand the machine provider description's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the name provider description's on descriptor 4, read from the person's vault, never in argv or a file. When a computer_row unit names a secret_vault_key, hand descriptor 5 one JSON object of each such vault name to the value the vault holds under it; the computer seals it with systemd-creds at the unit's secret_file. Tell the person the computer's public name, its price, what was built and whether its health page answered 200. If it stops part way, run the same command again: the saved lease resumes it.

payload.label: Rent a machine
payload.job: Rent a machine (or take one I already run) with a public name pointed at it, for another tool to set up
payload.description: Rents a machine from the provider description the request names (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through the name provider description, waits until it answers SSH, and answers the lease, the public name, the machine's architecture and the monthly price. It sets nothing up on the machine: another tool (an engine builder, a computer) does that. tool:give-back-a-computer gives it back from the same lease file. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

request_file.description: A request JSON (lease_file, machine, name, ssh); its paths are read relative to it.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Hand the machine provider description's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the name provider description's on descriptor 4, read from the person's vault, never in argv or a file. Tell the person the machine's public name, address and monthly price.

payload.label: Read a computer's price
payload.job: See what a machine for a computer would cost each month before renting it
payload.description: Reads the monthly price of the request's machine size at its location from the provider description's price request. Rents nothing.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider description's vault_key credential on descriptor 3. A null price means the description reads none (a machine the person already runs and gave no price for).

payload.label: Read a computer
payload.job: See whether a computer's machine is running and its health page answers
payload.description: Reads the saved lease, the machine's state at the provider and the health page's HTTP status at the computer's public name.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider description's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 (none for a machine the person already runs).

payload.label: Check a sign-up
payload.job: Prove a public address takes a new account end to end: sign up, sign in and read a signed-in page
payload.description: Signs up one synthetic account at the origin with a software passkey made for this run only, signs in with it under the new account's address, and reads a page only a signed-in person sees, then the same page without the session. Answers each step's HTTP status, the new address and whether the signed-in read answered 200. The passkey leaves with the process, so the synthetic account can never be signed in to again.

invoke.say: No credential is needed. Tell the person the new address and which step stopped, if one did. Each run leaves one synthetic account behind at the computer that took it; name it as synthetic wherever it is counted.

payload.label: Give back a computer
payload.job: Stop paying for a computer's machine: remove its public name and give the machine back
payload.description: Removes the public name the lease made, then deletes the machine and the SSH key the lease made, each only after reading it back and finding this lease's own label. A machine the person already runs is only forgotten, never touched. Move the computer's accounts to another computer first: this deletes the machine's disk.

invoke.say: Hand the machine provider description's vault_key credential on descriptor 3 and the name provider description's on descriptor 4. Confirm with the person that the computer holds no account that has not moved.
